extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (computer algebra) working with non-commutative/letterplace computations; mathematicians and computational algebra developers
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of Singular library procedures for letterplace/non‑commutative computations (usage, returns, assumptions, examples) used to transform between intvec/intmat/monomial representations, compute properties of quotient algebras, and compute Groebner bases and involutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivL2lpI
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming a list of intvecs into an ideal of Letterplace monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ivL2lpI(L); L a list of intvecs. Return: ideal. Purpose: Transforming a list of intvecs into an ideal of Letterplace monomials. Assume: Intvec corresponds to a Letterplace monomial; basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: Assumptions will not be checked! Example shows defining Letterplace ring and list L and ivL2lpI(L) returning an ideal of corresponding monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lp
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming an intvec into the corresponding Letterplace polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: iv2lp(I); I an intvec. Return: poly. Purpose: Transforming an intvec into the corresponding Letterplace polynomial. Assume: Intvec corresponds to a Letterplace monomial; basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: Assumptions will not be checked! Example demonstrates iv2lp(u) returning x(1)*x(2)*y(3), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lpList
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting a list of intmats into an ideal of corresponding monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: iv2lpList(L); L a list of intmats. Return: ideal. Purpose: Converting a list of intmats into an ideal of corresponding monomials. Assume: The rows of each intmat in L must correspond to a Letterplace monomial; basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Example shows intmats of different sizes, list L, and returned ideal of monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lpMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting an intmat into an ideal of the corresponding monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: iv2lpMat(M); M an intmat. Return: ideal. Purpose: Converting an intmat into an ideal of the corresponding monomials. Assume: The rows of M must correspond to Letterplace monomials; basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Example shows iv2lpMat applied to various intmats returning respective monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: lp2iv
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming a monomial into the corresponding intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lp2iv(p); p a poly. Return: intvec. Purpose: Transforming a monomial into the corresponding intvec. Assume: basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: Assumptions will not be checked! Example: lp2iv(p) returns sequences like 1,1,3 for x(1)*x(2)*z(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: lp2ivId
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting an ideal into a list of intmats whose rows are the corresponding intvecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lp2ivId(G); G an ideal. Return: list. Purpose: Converting an ideal into an list of intmats, the corresponding intvecs forming the rows. Assume: basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Example shows lp2ivId(G) returning list of intmats representing polynomials in G.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpId2ivLi
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming an ideal into the corresponding list of intvecs (as list of intvecs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpId2ivLi(G); G an ideal. Return: list. Purpose: Transforming an ideal into the corresponding list of intvecs. Assume: basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Example: returns intvecs such as 1,1 ; 2,2 ; 1,2,1 for ideal elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpNoetherian
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether R/<G> is noetherian (left/right/both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpNoetherian(G); G an ideal in a Letterplace ring. Return: int (0 not noetherian, 1 left noetherian, 2 right noetherian, 3 noetherian). Purpose: Check whether R/<G> is (left/right) noetherian, where R is the basering. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring; G is a Groebner basis. Example: lpNoetherian(G) → 2 for K<x,y>/<xx,yx>.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpIsSemiPrime
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether R/<G> is semiprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpIsSemiPrime(G); G an ideal in a Letterplace ring. Return: boolean. Purpose: Check whether R/<G> is semi prime, where R is the basering. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring; G is a Groebner basis. Example: lpIsSemiPrime(G) → 1 for K<x1,x2>/<x1*x2,x2*x1>.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpIsPrime
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether R/<G> is prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpIsPrime(G); G an ideal in a Letterplace ring. Return: boolean. Purpose: Check whether R/<G> is prime, where R is the basering. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring; G is a Groebner basis. Example: lpIsPrime(G) → 1 for K<x,y>/<xx,yy>.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpGkDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the Gelfand–Kirillov (GK) dimension of A/<G> (or -1 if infinite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpGkDim(G); G an ideal in a letterplace ring. Return: int (-1 means positive infinite). Purpose: Determines the Gelfand Kirillov dimension of A/<G>. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring; G is a Groebner basis. Example: various ideals produce -1, 0, 2 outputs; examples show ring construction and calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpGlDimBound
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute an upper bound for the global dimension of A/<I> (returns -1 if infinite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpGlDimBound(I); I an ideal. Return: int, an upper bound for the global dimension, -1 means infinity. Purpose: computing an upper bound for the global dimension. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring, G is a reduced Groebner Basis. Note: If I = LM(I), then the global dimension equals the GK dimension if finite. Examples and remarks: global dimension should be 0 for A/G = K and 1 for A/G = K<x1...xn>.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpSubstitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute lists/ideals of variables by polynomials in a letterplace polynomial (optional reduction by G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpSubstitute(f,s1,s2[,G]); f letterplace polynomial, s1 list (ideal) of variables to replace, s2 list (ideal) of polynomials to replace with, G optional ideal to reduce with. Return: poly, the substituted polynomial. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring; G is a Groebner basis; current ring has sufficient degbound (can be calculated with lpCalcSubstDegBound()). Note: Examples show computing minDegBound via lpCalcSubstDegBounds, constructing new Letterplace ring with that degbound, mapping objects into it, and invoking lpSubstitute; warnings in output about integer division in examples are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpCalcSubstDegBound
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the minimum degree bound (uptodeg) required to perform a substitution for a single polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpCalcSubstDegBound(f,s1,s2); f letterplace polynomial, s1 list (ideal) of variables to replace, s2 list (ideal) of polynomials to replace with. Return: int, the min degbound required to perform the substitution. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring. Example: see lpSubstitute examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpCalcSubstDegBounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the minimum degree bound required to perform a set of substitutions for a list/ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpCalcSubstDegBounds(I,s1,s2); I list (ideal) of letterplace polynomials, s1 list (ideal) of variables to replace, s2 list (ideal) of polynomials to replace with. Return: int, the min degbound required to perform all of the substitutions. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring. Note: convenience method; see lpSubstitute examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeLetterplaceRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a Letterplace ring with ordering and attributes used in letterplace computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: makeLetterplaceRing(d [,h]); d an integer, h an optional integer. Return: ring. Purpose: creates a ring with the ordering, used in letterplace computations. Notes on h: h=0 (default) uses Dp ordering; h=2 uses weights 1 for all variables and a tie breaker list of blocks of original ring; h=1 uses pure homogeneous letterplace block ordering (for homogeneous input ideals). Example shows constructing ring, attributes 'isLetterplaceRing', 'uptodeg', 'lV' and checking them.

rubrics_metrics.name: letplaceGBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal via the Letterplace algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: letplaceGBasis(I); I an ideal. Return: ideal. Assume: basering is a Letterplace ring, an ideal consists of Letterplace polynomials. Purpose: compute the two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal I via Letterplace algorithm. Note: degree bound for computation is read off the letterplace structure of basering. Example demonstrates letplaceGBasis(I) returning J with several letterplace polynomials; then conversion to free algebra strings via lp2lstr and lst2str.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpNF
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the normal form of a letterplace polynomial p with respect to a Letterplace Groebner basis G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpNF(p,G); p letterplace polynomial, ideal G. Return: poly. Purpose: computation of the normal form of p with respect to G. Assume: p is a Letterplace polynomial, G is a set of Letterplace polynomials being a Letterplace Groebner basis (no check). Note: Strategy: take the smallest monomial wrt ordering for reduction - for homogeneous ideals the shift does not matter; for non-homogeneous ideals the first shift will be the smallest monomial. Example: lpNF(p,J) returns reduced forms; lpNF(q,J) may return 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: setLetterplaceAttributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set letterplace attributes for a ring (isLetterplaceRing, uptodeg, lV) and return a ring with these attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: setLetterplaceAttributes(R, d, b); R a ring, b,d integers. Return: ring with special attributes set. Purpose: sets attributes: 'isLetterplaceRing' = true, 'uptodeg' = d, 'lV' = b ('uptodeg' degree bound; 'lV' number of variables in block 0). Note: Activate resulting ring with setring. Example shows attrib(R,'isLetterplaceRing') returns 1 after setting attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: freeGBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal encoded as a list of modules (representing free algebra polynomials) up to a given degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: freeGBasis(L, d); L a list of modules, d an integer. Return: ring. Assume: L has special form: each generator represents a monomial times coefficient in free algebra, the 1st entry is a nonzero coefficient from ground field, each next entry hosts a variable from basering. Purpose: compute two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal encoded by L in free associative algebra, up to degree d. Note: Apply lst2str to output for readable presentation. Example shows modules, list L, call freeGBasis(L,5), and conversion to readable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpMult
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the letterplace form of the product f*g of two letterplace polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpMult(f,g); f,g letterplace polynomials. Return: poly. Assume: basering has a letterplace ring structure. Purpose: compute the letterplace form of f*g. Example demonstrates lpMult(b,a) and lpMult(a,b) with differing outputs due to noncommutativity/shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: shiftPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the i-th shift of a letterplace polynomial p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: shiftPoly(p,i); p letterplace poly, i int. Return: poly. Assume: basering has letterplace ring structure. Purpose: compute the i-th shift of letterplace polynomial p. Example: shiftPoly(f,1) and shiftPoly(f,2) produce shifted variable indices (x(2),z(3),...).

rubrics_metrics.name: lpPower
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the letterplace form of f^n for a letterplace polynomial f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lpPower(f,n); f letterplace polynomial, int n. Return: poly. Assume: basering has a letterplace ring structure. Purpose: compute the letterplace form of f^n. Example: lpPower(a,2) and lpPower(b,4) show expanded shifted products.

rubrics_metrics.name: lieBracket
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the Lie bracket [a,b] = ab - ba (optionally left-normed iterated if N>1) between letterplace polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lieBracket(a,b[,N]); a,b letterplace polynomials, N optional integer. Return: poly. Assume: basering has a letterplace ring structure. Purpose: compute the Lie bracket [a,b] = ab - ba. Note: if N>1 is specified, compute left-normed bracket [a,[...[a,b]]]]. Example: lieBracket(a,b) returns -y(1)*x(2)*y(3)+x(1)*y(2)*y(3); lieBracket(x(1),y(1),2) returns a longer left-normed bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: lp2lstr
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert a letterplace ideal to a list of modules (export object @LN into a specified ring) for subsequent conversion to free algebra strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lp2lstr(K,s); K an ideal, s a ring name. Return: nothing (exports object @LN into ring named s). Assume: basering has a letterplace ring structure. Purpose: converts letterplace ideal to list of modules. Note: useful as preprocessing to 'lst2str'. Example: lp2lstr(I,r); setring r; lst2str(@LN,1) yields free algebra polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: lst2str
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert a list of modules into polynomials in the free algebra (strings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lst2str(L[,n]); L a list of modules, n optional integer. Return: list (of strings). Purpose: convert a list (of modules) into polynomials in free algebra. Note: if optional integer not 0, star signs are used in multiplication. Example shows conversion of modules to readable free algebra polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: mod2str
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert a module into a polynomial string in the free algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: mod2str(M[,n]); M a module, n optional integer. Return: string. Purpose: convert a module into a polynomial in free algebra. Note: if optional integer not 0, star signs are used in multiplication. Example: mod2str(M) -> 'xyxy-2yxyx+6xyyxy'; mod2str(M,1) -> 'x*y*x*y-...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: vct2str
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert a vector into a word (string) in the free algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: vct2str(v[,n]); v a vector, n optional integer. Return: string. Purpose: convert a vector into a word in free algebra. Note: if optional integer not 0, star signs used in multiplication. Examples show conversion with coefficients and powers, and with/without explicit stars.

rubrics_metrics.name: serreRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ideal of Serre relations associated to a generalized Cartan matrix A in letterplace form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: serreRelations(A,z); A an intmat, z an int. Return: ideal. Assume: basering has a letterplace ring structure and A is a generalized Cartan matrix with integer entries. Purpose: compute the ideal of Serre’s relations associated to A. Example: constructs Serre relations for given Cartan matrix and returns list of letterplace polynomials representing relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: fullSerreRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute inhomogeneous Serre relations associated to a Cartan matrix A given variable ideals for negative/positive roots and Cartan elements, returning a ring and the ideal 'fsRel'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: fullSerreRelations(A,N,C,P,d); A an intmat, N,C,P ideals, d an int. Return: ring (and ideal). Purpose: compute the inhomogeneous Serre’s relations associated to A in given variable names. Input ideals N (negative roots), P (positive roots), C (Cartan elements) must be of same sizes and contain variables interpreted accordingly. d is the degree bound for letterplace ring. Result is ideal called 'fsRel' in returned ring. Example demonstrates fsRel[1..17] for A_2.

rubrics_metrics.name: isVar
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the leading monomial of p is a power of a single basering variable; return exponent or 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isVar(p); poly p. Return: int. Purpose: check whether leading monomial of p is a power of a single variable from the basering. Returns the exponent or 0 if p is multivariate. Example: isVar(f) -> 0 for xy+1; isVar(g) -> 3 for y^3; isVar(i) -> 0 for 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ademRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ideal of Adem relations for i<2j in characteristic 0; exports ideal AdemRel in the output ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ademRelations(i,j); i,j int. Return: ring (and exports ideal). Assume: there are at least i+j variables in the basering. Purpose: compute the ideal of Adem relations for i<2j in characteristic 0. Example: def A = ademRelations(2,5); setring A; AdemRel yields relations like 6*s(7)*s(0)+s(6)*s(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: findInvo
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ideal of linear involutions of the basering and return a ring containing a list L of pairs (associated prime's Groebner basis, matrix defining linear map reduced wrt that prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: findInvo(); Return: a ring containing a list L of pairs where L[i][1]=ideal (Groebner basis of i-th associated prime), L[i][2]=matrix defining linear map with entries reduced wrt L[i][1]. Purpose: compute the ideal of linear involutions of the basering. Assume: relations on algebra are of the form YX = XY + D (current ring is a G-algebra of Lie type). Note: idJ and initial matrix matD are exported in output ring for convenience. Example: for first Weyl algebra findInvo() returns ring X with L listing matrices and associated ideals; prints show matrices and idJ relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: findInvoDiag
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute homothetic (diagonal) involutions of the basering, returning similar list of associated primes and diagonal matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: findInvoDiag(); Return: a ring together with a list L of pairs L[i][1]=ideal (Groebner basis), L[i][2]=matrix defining linear map. Purpose: compute homothetic (diagonal) involutions of the basering. Assume: relations are YX = XY + D (G-algebra of Lie type). Note: idJ and matD exported. Example: for Weyl algebra, finds constant diagonal matrices like diag(-1,1) and diag(1,-1) and prints idJ entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: findAuto
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ideal(s) of linear automorphisms of the basering whose n-th power is identity (unipotent if n specified; if n=0 look for all non-degenerate automorphisms), returning a ring and list of (prime ideal, defining matrix) pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: findAuto(n); n an integer. Return: a ring together with a list L where L[i][1]=ideal (Groebner basis), L[i][2]=matrix defining linear map reduced wrt that ideal. Purpose: compute ideal of linear automorphisms of basering given by matrices of order n. Assume: relations YX = XY + D (G-algebra of Lie type). Note: if n=0 matrix not assumed unipotent but non-degenerate; a nonzero parameter @p introduced as determinant. idJ and matD exported. Examples show findAuto(2) returning identity and diagonal -1 matrices; findAuto(0) returns parametrized family with @p as nonzero parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncdetection
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute classical involutions (acting on operators rather than variables) for certain noncommutative algebras arising in control theory; returns an ideal representing an involution map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ncdetection(); Return: ideal representing an involution map. Purpose: compute classical involutions for some particular noncommutative algebras (differential, shift or advance operators arising in Control Theory). Assume: procedure aimed at non-commutative algebras with differential, shift or advance operators; it has to be executed in a ring. Example: with ring R = 0,(x,y,z,D(1..3)),dp and appropriate nc_algebra setup, ncdetection() returns list of variables [x,y,z].
